F v. Pressure
The molecules of the gas are in continuous state of motion. They collide with
each other as well as with walls of the container. When the gas molecules
collide with walls of the container, they exert pressure on the walls of the
container. Force (F) exerted by a gas on per unit area (A) of a container is
called pressure (P).
P=F/A
The SI unit of force is Newton and that of area is m’. Hence, the SI unit of
pressure is N.m™. It is also called Pascal (Pa). Pascal is very small unit in
pressure measurement, usually its bigger form is kilo Pascal (kPa) is used.
At sea level at 0°C, the atmospheric pressure is 760 mm of Hg or 760 torr. It is
termed as one atmospheric pressure. So,
1 atmosphere = 760 mm of Hg
= 760 torr (1mm of Hg = 1 torr)
= 101.325 kPa
= 1.01325x 10’ Pa
vi. Compressibility
Gases are highly compressible. This is because that gases molecules have
large empty spaces. When the pressure is applied on the gases, the distance
between the molecules decreases, its volume also decreases. So the
compressibility of gases may be defined as, the change in volume per unit
change in pressure.
vii. Mobility
Molecules of the gases are in state of continuous motion because of the
weak intermolecular forces present between them. They move from one
place to another as they have weak intermolecular forces and empty spaces.
That is why, gases flow and can be transported through pipes over long
distances.
